findings.claim: The five new aliases are declared inside an `@theme inline` block but every migrated consumer references them as `var(--color-*)`, so the variables will not resolve at runtime and roughly 12 of the 29 migrated call sites render with invalid/unset colors.
findings.evidence: The tokens.css hunk header reads `@@ @theme inline semantic compatibility aliases` and adds `--color-terminal-fg: hsl(var(--terminal-fg));` etc. In Tailwind v4, `@theme inline` inlines theme values into generated utilities and does NOT emit the corresponding CSS custom properties; even if emitted at `:root`, `var(--terminal-fg)` would be resolved at `:root` where — per the design's own risk section — 'their current channel variables are scoped to the terminal theme', producing an invalid-at-computed-value-time result that inherits. Yet the diff migrates consumers to direct variable reads: `text-[var(--color-terminal-fg-dim)]` (loading-cursor.tsx, empty-frame.tsx), `var(--color-signal-red)`/`var(--color-phosphor-glow)` (error-bar.tsx), and `color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-terminal-fg) 6%, transparent)` (index.css scanline). These resolve to guaranteed-invalid, silently dropping colors. The verification evidence (`Vite 8.1.4 development compilation served main.tsx, tokens.css, and index.css successfully`) is compilation/HTTP-only and cannot detect unresolved custom properties, so the claimed 'Runtime UX: colors ... remain visually equivalent' and criterion 2.5 are unverified against rendered output.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not alias scoped channel variables through `@theme inline` for `var()` consumption. Define the five aliases as plain custom properties inside the same scope where `--terminal-fg`/`--signal-red`/etc. are defined (e.g., the terminal theme selector block: `--color-terminal-fg: hsl(var(--terminal-fg));`), so the var() chain resolves within scope, and verify with a computed-style check in the running app, not just compilation.

findings.claim: The deferred-scope gate hardcodes an exact count of 307 and scans `frontend/src/admin/pages` non-recursively, making it brittle against any legitimate future edit and blind to nested files.
findings.evidence: `const deferredCount = readdirSync(adminRoot).filter((file) => file.endsWith(".tsx")).reduce(...)` uses `readdirSync` without `{ recursive: true }`, so any `.tsx` files in subdirectories of `admin/pages` are silently excluded from the '307 deferred' proof, and `if (deferredCount !== 307)` will fail CI for any unrelated legitimate change to admin pages — including C-14a, which the proposal itself designates as the owner of those occurrences — until someone edits the magic number.
findings.suggested_fix: Scan recursively (or reuse whatever census method produced 307), and replace the exact-count equality with a check that C-05-owned files stay clean plus a documented, dated snapshot constant for the deferred set, or scope the 307 assertion to the C-05 phase only.

findings.claim: The legacy-syntax detector misses the `hsla(var(` variant, so the gate does not fully enforce the 'no legacy HSL-channel call site' contract it claims to own.
findings.evidence: `const legacyCall = /hsl\s*\(\s*var\s*\(/g;` matches only `hsl(`; a contributor adding `hsla(var(--muted) / 0.5)` to any of the six gated files would pass the gate even though the OpenSpec scenario requires the harness to reject legacy channel syntax in the migrated file set.
